goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds standalone assets `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` and `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss`, and the new layout `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb` calls `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'`. The diff does not show any change to an asset manifest (e.g., `application.css/js`) or to an assets precompile configuration to ensure `embed.css`/`embed.js` are compiled for production. If this app requires explicit precompile entries for non-application assets (common in Rails), `embed.css` would 404 in production.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:32 calls i.content.scrub on nil when a feed item has no content element, raising NoMethodError; with retry: false the whole feed poll dies silently and no subsequent items import
Migration modified to use force: true on create_table :top_topics (also duplicated in create_topic_embeds), a data-loss foot-gun if re-run against an existing table

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` (db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) and adds a new migration with `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` (db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb). In Rails, `force: true` will drop an existing table before creating it, which is a real data-loss risk if the migration is ever run when the table already exists (e.g., re-run, partial/failed previous run, or inconsistent environments). However, under normal Rails migration behavior, already-run migrations aren’t re-executed, so this is more a risky foot-gun than a guaranteed defect in typical operation.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `require_dependency 'nokogiri'` at the top of `app/models/topic_embed.rb`, and the file directly uses `Nokogiri::HTML.fragment(contents)` later, so it is not “dead weight.” Whether `require_dependency` vs `require` is preferable for a gem is, at most, a minor style/idiom concern and not a verifiable defect or important issue grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed crashes with NoMethodError when a feed item lacks content, aborting the entire import loop and silently skipping subsequent items due to retry: false

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop unconditionally does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item has no `content` (i.e., `i.content` is `nil`), calling `.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the entire `rss.items.each` import. The job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so a crash will not be retried and items after the failing one won't be imported in that run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS: PollFeed imports raw feed HTML with cook_method raw_html bypassing sanitization, and the embed view renders it with raw post.cooked, allowing malicious scripts from feeds

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows feed content is imported and stored as raw HTML without sanitization, then rendered unescaped. In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, it takes `i.content` (from `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`), does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and calls `TopicEmbed.import(...)`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates the first post via `PostCreator.new(... raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`. In `Post#cook`, `raw_html` returns `raw` directly, skipping the cooking/sanitization pipeline. Finally, `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` renders `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. This combination enables stored XSS if a feed item contains malicious HTML/JS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import interpolates the URL into HTML without escaping, allowing attribute breakout via crafted feed link values

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code builds HTML with `"#{url}"` and passes it into `I18n.t(...)`, then appends it directly to `contents` (which is later stored and rendered as `raw_html`). The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes/spaces. A crafted feed `link` like `http://example.com/' onmouseover='...` would match the regex and break out of the `href` attribute, enabling HTML/JS injection when the post is rendered (`post.cook_method == raw_html` and the embed view uses `<%= raw post.cooked %>`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: PostRevisor change to save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]) is a global behavior change affecting all callers with no verification for non-embed paths

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `PostRevisor#update_post` from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, which alters behavior for any caller that passes `skip_validations: true` (validations will now be skipped). The new embed/import path (`TopicEmbed.import` calling `revisor.revise!(..., skip_validations: true, ...)`) relies on this, but the diff does not show any tests or verification around how this affects other existing `PostRevisor` call sites that may also use `skip_validations`. This is a diff-grounded scope/behavior-change concern rather than a directly provable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key is dead code including unused require 'digest/sha1' since the conditional fetch requirement was dropped

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `require 'digest/sha1'` is only used by the `feed_key` method, but `feed_key` is never referenced anywhere in this diff (the job’s `execute` path calls `poll_feed`, which parses the feed and imports items without using `feed_key`). Based on the diff alone, this looks like dead/unused code rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Referer host comparison in EmbedController is exact-string, breaking www. subdomain and case variations

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the referer host is checked via exact equality: `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. This will reject embeddings when the referer is a different-but-related host (e.g., `www.example.com` vs `example.com`) unless the admin config exactly matches. The diff shows no normalization or allowance for subdomains, so the concern is grounded, but whether `www` should be permitted is a product/requirements decision rather than a definite defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: raw_html cook path silently skips Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook), so plugins don't run on feed-imported posts

adjudication.rationale: Verified: `Post#cook` now short-circuits for `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and returns `raw` immediately (`app/models/post.rb`), which means `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` is not executed for those posts. Feed-imported posts are explicitly created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (`TopicEmbed.import`), so plugins relying on `:after_post_cook` won’t run for imported content. This appears intentional (“skip the rendering pipeline”), but it is a real plugin-compatibility/behavioral concern introduced by the diff rather than a definitively unintended defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed/best crashes when the embedded topic has been deleted because TopicEmbed rows aren't pruned and there's no nil guard on the topic

adjudication.rationale: EmbedController#best trusts TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) and unconditionally does `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` when a topic_id is returned. TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed just plucks :topic_id from the topic_embeds row without verifying the Topic still exists, and the migration defines no FK/cleanup behavior for topic_embeds. If the Topic (or associated Post) is deleted while the TopicEmbed row remains, this path can raise (e.g., TopicView/topic lookup) or later fail when the view calls `@topic_view.topic`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import rewrite deletes the --category option and created_at backdating, breaking the documented -c flag and losing original creation dates

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor, the PR removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` and the associated `category_id` lookup/`category: category_id` parameter passed to `PostCreator`, so the `-c/--category` flag no longer exists or has any effect. It also replaces `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) ...)` with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which does not pass `created_at`, so imported topics/posts will no longer be backdated to the original Disqus thread creation time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: force: true added to create_top_topics migration drops and recreates top_topics data on existing environments

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the existing migration `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, which *would* drop/recreate the table if that migration were executed when the table already exists. However, the finding claims it "drops and recreates top_topics data on existing environments"—but from the diff alone we cannot verify that this migration will be re-run on existing environments (Rails migrations are normally run once and recorded in `schema_migrations`, so editing an old migration file does not automatically execute it again). Thus the asserted existing-environment data loss is not supported by what the diff shows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New embed settings in site_settings.yml are not marked client: true, so no admin UI renders and the feature is unusable without console access

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `embedding:` section in `config/site_settings.yml` with four new settings, and also adds the admin category label (`js.admin.site_settings.categories.embedding`) in `config/locales/client.en.yml`, indicating intent for these to appear in the admin UI. From the diff alone, there is no evidence that omitting `client: true` prevents admin UI rendering; in Discourse, `client: true` typically controls exposure to the client app at runtime, not whether a setting is editable in the admin interface. The claim that the feature is unusable without console access is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.permalink locale key is defined but never referenced anywhere, shipping a dead translation key

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `embed.permalink` under `config/locales/server.en.yml`, and there is no visible reference to `I18n.t('embed.permalink')` (or equivalent) in the added embed views/controllers/jobs. However, an unused locale key is a minor maintenance nit rather than a verifiable defect or important review issue based on this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_url is never validated against embeddable_host in EmbedController's synchronous render path; only TopicRetriever enforces it on creation, so content can be served for any embed_url origin

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, the only host check is in `ensure_embeddable`, which validates `request.referer` host against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (and sets `X-Frame-Options`). The `embed_url` param itself is only `params.require(:embed_url)` and is then used to look up an existing `TopicEmbed` via `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)`; if found, it renders synchronously via `TopicView.new(...)` with no validation that `URI(embed_url).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Therefore, if a `TopicEmbed` exists for some other host (e.g., created via feed import / other paths), the allowed embedding host can request and serve that content by passing that `embed_url`, even though the `embed_url` origin doesn’t match the configured embeddable host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed/best.html.erb else-branch evaluates @topic_view.topic.url without a nil guard, risking NoMethodError instead of a 4xx error when @topic_view is nil

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no topic_id is found it explicitly `render 'loading'` and does not render `embed/best.html.erb`. The `best.html.erb` template is only used in the branch where `@topic_view = TopicView.new(...)` is set, so `@topic_view` will not be nil when that template runs based on the diff shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_url written by feed importer and looked up by embed controller are not canonicalized/normalized (no trailing slash, scheme, or query param handling), causing exact-match lookup failures, duplicate topic creation, or endless reload loop

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows embed lookups are exact string matches on `embed_url` with no normalization: `EmbedController#best` calls `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` which does `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: embed_url)`; `TopicRetriever` also checks `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`. Meanwhile, different ingestion paths can store different URL variants for the same page (`PollFeed` uses `i.link` or `i.id`; `embed.js` passes `discourseEmbedUrl` from the embedding page, which may include/omit trailing slash, query params, etc.). With a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, this can lead to duplicate topics for URL variants, and if the stored URL differs from the requested one, `best` will keep rendering `loading` and reloading every 30s because it never finds a matching `TopicEmbed` row.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb compares request referer host to SiteSetting.embeddable_host as exact string without validation/normalization; admin entering different casing or scheme causes all embeds to 403 with no feedback

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the diff adds a strict equality check `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. This compares the parsed referer host string directly against the raw site setting without any normalization (e.g., downcasing) or parsing of the setting (e.g., if an admin enters `https://example.com` instead of `example.com`). Since hostnames are case-insensitive and the setting has no shown validation/normalization in this diff, legitimate embeds can be rejected with `Discourse::InvalidAccess` ('invalid referer host').

adjudication_records.issue_text: Two parallel hand-maintained host validators (embed_controller and TopicRetriever#invalid_host?) with no shared normalization helper drift in behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces two separate host checks with similar intent but different inputs and error handling: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` compares `URI(request.referer || '').host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and treats blank setting as an error, while `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` compares `URI(@embed_url).host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and rescues `URI::InvalidURIError` to return `true`. There is no shared normalization/helper, so future changes to what constitutes a valid embeddable host (case, ports, subdomains, blank handling) could easily drift between these two locations. This is an architectural/maintainability issue evidenced by the duplicated logic, not an immediate functional defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: perform_retrieve synchronously runs a full PollFeed (blocking network fetch and bulk import of all feed items) to satisfy a single embed page view, flooding Sidekiq/DB and potentially blocking a worker indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline (not enqueued). `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` does a blocking `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` network fetch and then iterates `rss.items.each` importing each item via `TopicEmbed.import`, which can create/update many topics/posts in one run. This can make a single `RetrieveTopic` job (triggered by an embed request) do an unbounded amount of work and potentially block a Sidekiq worker; however it’s not strictly a correctness defect visible in the diff, more a scope/performance/architecture concern. (Also, it’s not run synchronously in the controller; it runs in the enqueued `RetrieveTopic` job.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb calls CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) which raises NoMethodError on feed items without content (nil), and with no per-item error isolation the exception poisons the whole poll run, skipping all subsequent items every hourly run
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same root problem: the code calls `i.content.scrub` (and then `CGI.unescapeHTML`) assuming `i.content` is always present, but many feed items have `content == nil`, causing a NoMethodError/nil dereference and crashing the poll run. The candidate adds extra detail about lack of per-item isolation but still targets the same underlying issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Check-then-insert race in TopicEmbed.import: two concurrent RetrieveTopic jobs for the same URL both pass the exists? check and one fails with ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, causing a spurious Sidekiq failure and a duplicated remote page fetch

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a classic check-then-insert race around the unique `topic_embeds.embed_url` index. In `TopicEmbed.import`, it does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if blank enters a transaction and calls `TopicEmbed.create!(embed_url: url, ...)` (db migration adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`). Two concurrent callers for the same URL can both observe `embed.blank?` and then one will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` on `create!`, with no rescue shown. Independently, `TopicRetriever.perform_retrieve` also does an `exists?` check before `fetch_http`, which can allow duplicate remote fetches if called concurrently (throttling can be bypassed via `no_throttle`, e.g., staff user in `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: best.html.erb calls post.user.small_avatar_url/username without nil guard or includes; a post whose author was deleted raises NoMethodError making the embed render a permanent 500

adjudication.rationale: In the new `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, the template directly dereferences `post.user.small_avatar_url` and `post.user.username` with no nil-guard. If `post.user` can ever be nil (e.g., due to deleted/missing user rows), this would raise `NoMethodError` and break embed rendering. The diff doesn’t establish whether `post.user` is guaranteed non-nil in all cases, so the 500 is plausible but not strictly verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embeds has no FK on topic_id/post_id and no dependent destroy, so deleting a topic/post leaves an orphan row that makes topic_id_for_embed return a dead topic_id and breaks every embed render

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `topic_embeds` with `topic_id`/`post_id` integer columns but no foreign keys (migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` only adds a unique index on `embed_url`) and the `TopicEmbed` model has plain `belongs_to :topic`/`:post` with no shown dependent cleanup on the owning `Topic`/`Post`. `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` blindly plucks `:topic_id`, and `EmbedController#best` will pass that id into `TopicView.new` if present. If the referenced topic/post is deleted, an orphan `topic_embeds` row can persist and cause embeds to look up a non-existent topic id, leading to broken/erroneous embed rendering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key in poll_feed.rb is dead code computing a cache key nothing reads or writes, misleadingly suggesting conditional-fetch support that doesn't exist

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` is defined to compute a Redis/cache key (`"feed-modified:..."`) but nothing in this diff calls `feed_key` or uses that key to read/write conditional fetch state. The actual `poll_feed` implementation always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates items unconditionally. This is dead/misleading code, but not a functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import mutates contents (appending the 'Imported from' footer) before computing content_sha1, so changes to the imported_from locale string trigger a full re-revision of every imported feed item on the next poll

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the method appends a localized footer to `contents` (`contents << "...#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', ...)}..."`) and then computes `content_sha1 = Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)`. Because the SHA is based on the post body *including* the locale-dependent string, changing `embed.imported_from` in `server.en.yml` would change the computed SHA even if the feed’s actual content is unchanged, causing the `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1` branch to run and `PostRevisor#revise!` to update/revise imported posts on the next poll. This is a concrete diff-grounded behavior, but it’s more of an avoidable churn/performance/design issue than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import task's --category/-c option was silently deleted, breaking existing operator invocations and causing imported threads to land in the default category instead of the configured one

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` line is removed, along with all logic that resolves `category_id` and passes `category: category_id` into `PostCreator`. The import path now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`TopicEmbed.import` do not accept or set a category. This verifiably breaks existing invocations that used `--category/-c` and changes where imported topics will be created (no longer honoring the requested category).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import path changed from PostCreator with a one-line permalink post to TopicEmbed.import_remote which fetches and scrapes the full remote page as raw HTML, and fails when thread links are unreachable or non-HTML

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` to call `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)` instead of creating a local post with just a permalink. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` and passes the result to `Readability::Document.new(...)` with no error handling. If `t[:link]` is unreachable or `open` fails, the import will raise and can abort processing, whereas the prior implementation did not depend on fetching the remote page. This failure mode is directly implied by the new code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration create_top_topics changed to force: true, making it destructive by dropping and recreating the top_topics table and wiping accumulated metrics on environments that already ran the original migration

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` in `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop an existing `top_topics` table before recreating it, which is potentially destructive if this migration is executed on a DB where that table already exists. However, the finding’s specific claim about wiping metrics on environments that already ran the original migration is not directly supported by the diff, since migrations normally don’t re-run once marked applied.

adjudication_records.issue_text: raw_html cook path removes the core sanitization invariant of the post pipeline, storing unsanitized RSS feed and Readability-scraped content in cooked and rendering it raw in embed/best.html.erb, enabling stored malicious HTML (P0 severity)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `:raw_html` cook path that bypasses the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (`Post#cook` returns `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` and sets `raw` to `absolutize_urls(url, contents)` where `contents` comes from RSS (`Jobs::PollFeed`: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) or Readability HTML (`TopicEmbed.import_remote`: `doc.content`). No sanitization is performed in `absolutize_urls` beyond rewriting relative `href/src`. The embed view then renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, which will emit any malicious HTML/attributes present in the imported content (especially via RSS path), enabling stored XSS. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: post_revisor change from @post.save to @post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]) alters the revisor's contract for all existing callers, silently skipping ActiveRecord validations for any caller passing skip_validations: true

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change behavior in `PostRevisor#update_post` from `@post.save` (always runs validations) to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, meaning any caller passing `skip_validations: true` will now bypass ActiveRecord validations. That is a contract/behavior change for existing callers (even if aligned with the option name), and it happens silently for those callers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS in topic_embed.rb: remote HTML imported via Readability without scheme validation, so javascript:/data: hrefs in whitelisted tags persist and are rendered with `raw post.cooked`

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a raw-HTML rendering path for imported content: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses `Readability::Document` to extract HTML (`doc.content`) with allowed tags/attributes including `a[href]` and `img[src]`, then `TopicEmbed.import` stores it via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In `Post#cook`, `raw_html` returns `raw` directly (skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline), and `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Nothing in `import_remote`, `import`, or `absolutize_urls` filters/normalizes dangerous URL schemes like `javascript:`/`data:` in `href`/`src`, so a stored XSS vector is plausibly introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unescaped interpolation of `url` into HTML in the `<hr><small>` footer in topic_embed.rb, allowing attribute injection via URLs like `http://x/'onmouseover='alert(1)` that pass the ^https?:// regex

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/topic_embed.rb`, `import` appends HTML containing `"#{url}"` into `contents` without escaping `url` (and only checks `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`). Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for that method, and the embed view renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, a crafted URL containing quotes (e.g., `http://x/'onmouseover='alert(1)`) can break out of the `href` attribute and inject arbitrary attributes/HTML, leading to XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb relies solely on the spoofable Referer header as the gate on /embed/best, allowing unauthenticated attackers to enumerate and read embedded topics

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access to `/embed/best` is gated by comparing `URI(request.referer || '').host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, and then setting `X-Frame-Options = "ALLOWALL"`. Since `request.referer` is derived from the client-controlled `Referer` header, a direct request can spoof this header to pass the check and reach `best`, which renders a `TopicView` for an existing embed (`TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)`). This is a security weakness introduced by the diff: authorization is based solely on a spoofable header.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb constructs TopicView without guardian/category-security checks, leaking posts from restricted categories to anonymous users

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, the code does `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` (passing `current_user`, which is the normal hook for permission/guardian checks in Discourse). The diff does not show `TopicView` bypassing security or returning posts from restricted categories to anonymous users, so an actual data leak is not verifiable from this PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js uses substring match `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` for origin checking, bypassable via domain-suffix tricks like forum.example.com.attacker.com
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that using indexOf/substring matching for origin validation is insecure and can be bypassed with crafted domains that include the expected domain as a substring (e.g., evil-discourseUrl.com or forum.example.com.attacker.com).

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.html.erb bakes the attacker-influenced request.referer into the postMessage target origin, allowing the resize message to target arbitrary parent origins

adjudication.rationale: In layouts/embed.html.erb the code uses `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`, but the controller’s `ensure_embeddable` guard enforces `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and rejects missing/invalid referers. That means an attacker cannot cause the target origin to be an arbitrary parent origin; it is constrained to the configured embeddable host. (There may be a separate correctness concern that `postMessage` expects an origin, not a full referer URL with path, but the finding’s claimed arbitrary-origin security issue is not supported by the diff.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb passes RSS item content to TopicEmbed.import with zero HTML filtering, widening the stored XSS surface (also feed_polling_url has no scheme restriction, permitting http/MITM)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` is passed directly into `TopicEmbed.import(...)` with no sanitization. `TopicEmbed.import` then creates/updates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for `raw_html`, skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The embed view renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so any HTML/JS from the feed can be stored and served, widening XSS risk. Additionally, `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` accepts `http` URLs with no scheme/https enforcement, which enables MITM tampering of feed content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller_spec.rb:10-20: '404 without embed_url' and 'missing host' tests fail in ensure_embeddable_host before params.require(:embed_url) is reached, so they pass regardless of whether the embed_url requirement exists — false-confidence assertions

adjudication.rationale: EmbedController has `before_filter :ensure_embeddable`, and `ensure_embeddable` raises when `SiteSetting.embeddable_host.blank?` or when `request.referer` is missing/invalid, before the action runs. In `EmbedController#best`, `params.require(:embed_url)` is inside the action, so the spec `it "is 404 without an embed_url" do; get :best; ... end` can fail due to `ensure_embeddable` (e.g., default `embeddable_host: ''` and no referer) without ever exercising the missing-`embed_url` path. This makes that test a false-confidence assertion about `params.require(:embed_url)` rather than a product bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller_spec.rb:52-56: TopicView mock returns nil and success assertion lives in shared after block; test never checks return value or rendered output, so a broken success path (e.g. best view crashing) still passes

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, the “creates a topic view when a topic_id is found” example only sets an expectation on `TopicView.new` and doesn’t stub a return value. In typical controller specs (no `render_views` shown), the view isn’t rendered, so even if `@topic_view` were `nil` and `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` would crash on `@topic_view.posts`, the spec would still pass because it only asserts `response` success and `X-Frame-Options` in the shared `after` block. This is a concrete test-coverage gap rather than an application defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller_spec.rb:47-51: 'tells the topic retriever to work' test stubs TopicRetriever but never asserts the enqueued retrieve_topic job received the correct embed_url (or user_id) argument

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: ...)` when no topic is found; it does not instantiate `TopicRetriever` or call `retrieve`. However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` ("tells the topic retriever to work...") stubs `TopicRetriever.new` and expects `retriever.retrieve` to be called. This is a verifiable mismatch that would make the test fail, and it also means the spec is not asserting the actual behavior (job enqueue/args).

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_retriever_spec.rb:33-42: all valid-host tests stub retrieved_recently?, so the new throttle logic ($redis.setnx/expire 60s, no_throttle bypass) has zero coverage; a regression in the redis key format or expiry would silently lock or disable retrieval with no failing spec

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb`, the “valid host” examples (lines ~33-42 in the new file) explicitly stub `retrieved_recently?` to return true/false, so they never exercise the newly added throttle implementation in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` (the `$redis.setnx`/`expire 60` key `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` and the `@opts[:no_throttle]` bypass added in `lib/topic_retriever.rb`). This leaves the redis key format/expiry and no_throttle behavior untested, which is a concrete test coverage gap tied to the new logic (not a functional defect by itself).

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_retriever_spec.rb (whole file): perform_retrieve's decision tree is only checked via boolean expects counts; no test runs it with real state, so wrong-URL fetches, fetching when embed exists, or import_remote with wrong user pass the suite

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb`, the tests only assert whether `perform_retrieve` is called (or not) based on stubbing `retrieved_recently?` and `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. No spec exercises `perform_retrieve`’s real branches in `lib/topic_retriever.rb` (early return when `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`, feed polling path via `Jobs::PollFeed`, or `fetch_http`’s lookup of `SiteSetting.embed_by_username` and subsequent `TopicEmbed.import_remote`). As a result, regressions in those branches could pass the suite. This is a concrete test-coverage gap for newly added nontrivial logic, not a verifiable runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed_spec.rb:7-40: only guard settings and poll_feed invocation are tested; SimpleRSS parsing, i.link/i.id https fallback, CGI.unescapeHTML content scrub, and TopicEmbed.import have no test coverage

adjudication.rationale: In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb the tests only assert that `execute` gates on `feed_polling_enabled?`, `feed_polling_url`, and `embed_by_username`, and that it delegates to `poll_feed` (via `poller.expects(:poll_feed)`). None of the new nontrivial logic inside `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` is exercised: `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`, per-item URL selection (`i.link` with fallback to `i.id` when blank or non-http(s)), `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and the call to `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed_spec.rb:45-47: 'Supports updating the post' asserts cooked matches 'new contents' which trivially matches because cooked == raw for raw_html posts; never asserts embed.content_sha1 was updated, so dropping update_column would cause endless hourly re-revisions undetected

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, updates are gated by `if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1` and then persist the new digest via `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`. The spec case `"Supports updating the post"` only asserts `post.cooked` matches `/new contents/`, but for imported posts `cook_method` is set to `:raw_html` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly (`return raw if cook_method == ...`). So the assertion doesn’t meaningfully verify the revisor path, nor does it assert that `embed.content_sha1` was updated. This is a diff-grounded test gap: removing `update_column` would not be caught and could cause repeated revisions on subsequent polls/imports.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed_spec.rb:38: post.cooked.start_with? should be an equality assertion; the prefix form silently tolerates trailing garbage appended by absolutize_urls

adjudication.rationale: The cited line in `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` intentionally uses `start_with?` to avoid brittle exact-string matching after `Nokogiri::HTML.fragment(contents).to_html` normalization in `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`. The finding’s claim that this “silently tolerates trailing garbage appended by absolutize_urls” is speculative and not a verifiable defect from the diff; it’s essentially a test-style preference rather than a concrete, diff-demonstrated problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed_spec.rb .import context: no test covers the unchanged-content path (content_sha1 == embed.content_sha1 → no revision) nor the post.present? failure branch, so skip-revision-when-unchanged behavior is unverified

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/topic_embed.rb` `.import`, the update path explicitly skips revising when `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1` is false (i.e., unchanged content), and there is also a `post.present?` guard after `creator.create` in the creation transaction. The added spec `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` covers malformed URL, the new-URL creation path, and the changed-content update path (`"Supports updating the post"`), but it does not exercise (1) the no-op branch when `content_sha1` is unchanged, nor (2) the creation branch where `creator.create` returns nil causing the guarded `TopicEmbed.create!` to be skipped. This is a concrete missing-test gap for newly added logic, not a demonstrated defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_table :topic_embeds uses force: true in migration 20131217174004, which silently drops the table and loses all embed-to-topic mappings if the migration re-runs

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb the migration calls `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`. In Rails this will drop the existing `topic_embeds` table if it already exists before recreating it, which would erase all embed_url/topic_id mappings on a re-run (e.g., rollback + re-migrate, or if the table exists for any reason). This is a real data-loss risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: force: true was added to the already-shipped create_top_topics migration in this diff, risking loss of all top_topics aggregate data on re-run or restore-from-dump

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists when this migration runs, which can erase existing `top_topics` aggregate data in scenarios where the migration is re-executed (e.g., rollback/redo, or environments where the table exists but the migration isn't recorded as applied).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import switched to TopicEmbed.import_remote no longer preserves original thread created_at or requested category, causing imported topics to have wrong dates and no category

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor, the previous import path used PostCreator.new(..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id). The diff removes the :category option entirely and replaces topic creation with TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title]). TopicEmbed.import_remote/TopicEmbed.import create posts via PostCreator without passing created_at or category, so imports will default to current timestamps and default category, no longer preserving the Disqus thread date or requested category.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embeds topic_id/post_id have no foreign-key constraints or dependent cleanup, so deleting a topic leaves dangling references that crash the PollFeed job with NoMethodError via PostRevisor.new(nil), permanently stopping feed imports

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `topic_embeds` with `topic_id`/`post_id` columns but no foreign keys, and the model has only `belongs_to :topic`/`:post` without any dependent cleanup shown. In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing embed is found it does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally `PostRevisor.new(post)` if the content changed; if `embed.post` is nil (e.g., the post/topic was deleted while the `topic_embeds` row remains), this will raise (nil deref) and would break callers like `Jobs::PollFeed` that iterate and import items. The specific claim about deletions definitely happening isn't fully provable from this diff, but the nil-crash path on dangling references is grounded in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: content_sha1 is committed via update_column even when the post revision fails to save, causing subsequent polls to permanently skip the update with no error surfaced

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing embed’s content changes, it calls `revisor.revise!(...)` and then unconditionally does `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). `PostRevisor#revise!` does not check whether `@post.save(...)` succeeded (lib/post_revisor.rb), and with `skip_validations: true` it saves with `validate: false` but can still fail (e.g., DB/callback issues). If the save fails, `content_sha1` is still updated, so subsequent polls will see matching SHA and permanently skip applying the content update.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PostRevisor.new(post) raises NoMethodError when embed.post is nil (dangling post_id), crashing the PollFeed job mid-feed with retry disabled

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, when an existing embed is found it does `post = embed.post` and, if the SHA changed, unconditionally calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` / `revisor.revise!` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). Since the migration adds `topic_embeds.post_id` without a foreign key, a dangling `post_id` (e.g., deleted post) would make `embed.post` nil; PostRevisor then dereferences `@post` (`@post.acting_user = ...`), causing a NoMethodError and crashing the job. Jobs::PollFeed has `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so a single bad embed would abort the feed poll mid-run without retries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Nil i.content in poll_feed.rb causes .scrub to raise NoMethodError, aborting the entire feed poll mid-iteration with partial import and no signal of skipped items

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the code unconditionally does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item lacks a `content` field (i.e., `i.content` is `nil`, which is plausible for RSS/Atom entries that only provide `description`/`summary`), calling `.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError` and abort the job mid-iteration, potentially causing partial imports.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No nil-guard on i.title in poll_feed.rb, feeding PostCreator a nil title with skip_validations: true

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, each RSS item calls `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)` with no fallback if `i.title` is nil/blank. In `TopicEmbed.import`, that `title` is passed directly into `PostCreator.new(... title: title, ... skip_validations: true ...)`. If a feed item lacks a title, this can attempt to create a topic/post with a nil/blank title (or raise due to downstream requirements), and there is no nil-guard or default title in the new code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-URL throttle on embed_url is trivially bypassed by varying the path component, enabling unbounded job enqueue and outbound fetch amplification on an unauthenticated endpoint

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, which throttles by a Redis key derived from the full `embed_url` string (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`) and only for 60 seconds. In `EmbedController#best`, when no existing `TopicEmbed` is found it enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` for the supplied `embed_url` without authentication. Because the throttle is per-exact-URL, a caller can bypass it by varying the path/query of `embed_url` on the same allowed host (the only host-level check is `invalid_host?` comparing `URI(@embed_url).host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`). Each unique `embed_url` will enqueue a new job and can trigger `open(url)` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, enabling unbounded job creation/outbound fetches within the configured host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RetrieveTopic silently does nothing when embed_by_username is unset, user doesn't exist, URL scheme isn't http, or host check fails, leaving the user in an infinite reload loop with no error surfaced

adjudication.rationale: The embed flow can get stuck rendering `embed/loading` (which reloads every 30s) when no TopicEmbed is ever created. `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` and renders `loading` when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` is nil. In `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, retrieval is skipped entirely if `invalid_host?` is true (e.g., `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` mismatches `URI(@embed_url).host`), with no signal back to the user. Even when host is valid, `fetch_http` returns early if `embed_by_username` doesn’t map to a user (`user.blank?`), again silently resulting in no embed. Additionally, `TopicEmbed.import` returns nil for non-http(s) URLs, so `import_remote` can end up doing nothing for such URLs. These cases leave the iframe page repeatedly reloading without surfacing an error, matching the finding’s core concern (though if `embed_by_username` is actually nil, `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` would likely raise rather than silently no-op).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Outbound fetches (open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url), open(url).read) have no open_timeout/read_timeout and no size cap, allowing a slow host to block Sidekiq workers indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces outbound network fetches using `open-uri` without any timeouts or response size limits: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` and `open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (`app/models/topic_embed.rb`). These run inside Sidekiq jobs (`Jobs::PollFeed`, `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` via `TopicRetriever`) and can block workers indefinitely on slow/unresponsive hosts, creating a real availability issue introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Readability::Document receives the entire unbounded download into memory

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the code does `open(url).read` and passes the full string to `Readability::Document.new(...)` (see `app/models/topic_embed.rb`). `open-uri` with `.read` will buffer the entire HTTP response into memory with no size limit, so a very large (or intentionally huge) page can cause excessive memory usage/DoS when embedding/importing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: post.present? is checked but post.persisted? is not, so TopicEmbed.create! can run with topic_id: nil and raise inside the transaction on failed post creation

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the creation branch does `post = creator.create` and then only guards with `if post.present?` before calling `TopicEmbed.create!(topic_id: post.topic_id, post_id: post.id, ...)`. If `PostCreator#create` can return a non-nil `Post` object that is not persisted (e.g., save failed), `post.id`/`post.topic_id` could be nil and the `create!` would raise due to DB `null: false` constraints. The diff doesn’t show `PostCreator#create`’s return semantics, so this is a defensiveness/edge-case concern rather than a clearly verifiable bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key in poll_feed.rb is dead code: computed but never read or written, implying caching that doesn't exist

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the method `feed_key` computes and memoizes a Redis-style key (`"feed-modified:#{Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(...)}`) but nothing in this diff ever calls `feed_key`, nor is that key written/read anywhere else in the shown changes. The polling logic always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` without any conditional based on last-modified/etag/cached state, so the method is currently dead code and suggests an unfinished caching/throttling mechanism.
